question: Who has written the book ‘Parliament: Powers, Functions & Privileges; A Comparative Constitutional Perspective’, launched by the former Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar in January 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. KS Chauhan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book **‘Parliament: Powers, Functions & Privileges; A Comparative Constitutional Perspective’** was authored by **Dr. KS Chauhan**.
 
• This book was launched by the former Vice-President of India, **Jagdeep Dhankhar**, in **January 2025**.
 
• It discusses the **powers, functions, and privileges** of the Parliament of India and provides a **comparative perspective** with other countries' constitutional frameworks.
 
• The book is particularly significant for understanding the **role and responsibilities of the Indian Parliament** in the context of democracy and governance.
 
• It is a valuable resource for researchers, academicians, and students studying the **Indian Constitution and political system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **MJ Akbar**__

 __
 
• **MJ Akbar** is a renowned Indian journalist, author, and politician.
 
• He has authored several books, including **‘India: The Siege Within’** and **‘The Shade of Swords’**.
 
• His works primarily focus on **Indian politics, history, and international relations**.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Rajen Saikia**__
 __
 
• **Dr. Rajen Saikia** is an academician and author specializing in Indian history and culture.
 
• His notable works include writings on the **history and socio-cultural developments of Assam**.
 
 
 
• **K Natwar Singh**__
 
 
• **K Natwar Singh** is a veteran Indian diplomat, politician, and writer.
 
• He has penned several books, including his autobiography, **‘One Life is Not Enough’**, which provides insights into Indian politics and diplomacy.
 
• He served as the **External Affairs Minister of India** from 2004 to 2005.
